Voiced stop, Voice stop (Phon.), a stopped consonant made with tone from the larynx while the mouth organs are closed at some point; a sonant mute, as b, d, g hard.
volunteernavy: A navy of vessels fitted out and manned by volunteers who sail under the flag of the regular navy and subject to naval discipline. Prussia in 1870, in the Franco-German war, organized such a navy, which was commanded by merchant seamen with temporary commissions, with the claim (in which England acquiesced) that it did not come within the meaning of the term privateer.
volcanize: To subject to, or cause to undergo, volcanic heat, and to be affected by its action.
vomition: The act or power of vomiting. Grew.
vowel: A vocal, or sometimes a whispered, sound modified by resonance in the oral passage, the peculiar resonance in each case giving to each several vowel its distinctive character or quality as a sound of… | Of or pertaining to a vowel; vocal.
volage: Light; giddy. (old) They wroughten all their lust volage. Chaucer.
volubility: The quality or state of being voluble (in any of the senses of the adjective).
vomito: The yellow fever in its worst form, when it is usually attended with black vomit. See Black vomit.
vomitive: Causing the ejection of matter from the stomach; emetic.
volost: In the greater part of Russia, a division for local government consisting of a group of mirs, or village communities; a canton.
vocabulist: The writer or maker of a vocabulary; a lexicographer.
